summary: Iteration 110: one frontend QA pass on the 62-day streak polish. No backend rerun, as requested. Setup was the same as iteration 109 and test-only: the existing bridge iso_bridge_streak_iter109.py on 127.0.0.1:8765, a separate test DB (tejas_isolated_iter105_test), a frozen clock per user, mocked auth/session returning a plain {user}, and Playwright sending /api/** to the bridge with the x-test-user header. Test users: seven, missed, full and pre. All 4 polish items PASS: (1) the dialog no longer collapses when it closes, (2) reduced motion covers the dialog, its overlay and the compact card, and the series explainer is unaffected, (3) all streak labels are at least 11px with no horizontal overflow or clipping at 1920x800 and 390x844, and the prelaunch cup is dimmed, (4) the compact card reads 'Start a new streak' when the current streak is 0. Light and dark themes both checked. Bridge stopped, test DB dropped, customer DB has 0 TEST_U_ attempt docs.

issues: Cosmetic only, nothing is clipped: in the 180px hero column, the label 'THE FINISH IS WORTH IT' wraps and leaves 'IT' alone on the second line. Optional fix: a slightly smaller letter-spacing or text-wrap:balance.
Cosmetic only, nothing is clipped: in the 5 narrow cards '15 days', '30 days' and similar wrap onto 2 lines, and 'Champion' fills its card edge to edge. Acceptable.

verified.dialog_close: Sampled every animation frame after clicking Back to my journey. Celebration (Bronze cup): 13 frames over about 225ms, data-state=closed, height 421 to 400px (zoom-out), and the title and description stayed in every frame, then the dialog unmounted. Silver cup (locked): smallest height during close was 419px, with its text intact. Reopening switches the content correctly: Silver cup (locked copy, no confetti), then Champion cup, then 'Day 3 · 3 Dec' (link /results/TEST_A_seven_2026-12-03), then Bronze cup opened by hand (18 confetti pieces). After closing, nothing stale stays in the DOM. Code review: when the user changes, the streak data is null and the section unmounts, which throws away the cached selection, so the earlier state cannot carry over.
verified.reduced_motion: With emulate_media reduced_motion=reduce: .streak-dialog, .streak-dialog-overlay, the dialog cup, the runner, the track fill, the runner position, the hero cup and the cup cards all show animation none, 0s, and transition 0s. Confetti is display:none. The dialog is gone 60ms after close. The .streak-mini card shows transition 0s. With no preference set, the enter animation, cup-arrive/float and confetti all run normally. The series explainer (series-about) opens and closes normally; its overlay keeps the default bg-black/80 classes, with no streak-dialog-overlay class added.
verified.typography_overflow: Checked text and element bounds inside streak-journey (day record expanded) and streak-mini-link for seven, missed, full and pre at 390x844, and for seven, missed and pre at 1920x800. Every result: smallest font 11px, 0 elements under 11px, 0 scroll overflow, 0 elements spilling outside the container, document overflow 0.
verified.copy: Compact card: missed (current 0, best 8) shows 'Start a new streak'; seven shows '7-day streak'; full shows '62-day streak'; pre shows 'Your 62-day run starts 1 Dec'. All link to /series/all-india-jee#my-streak. The prelaunch hero cup has opacity 0.5 and saturate(0.5), with the label 'THE FINISH IS WORTH IT'.
verified.themes: Dark theme: the hub and the pending dialog ('Day 13 · 13 Dec', Open result) are readable (background rgb(21,17,20), text rgb(246,247,249), description rgb(192,198,206)).

action_items: None required. Optional cosmetic: balance the wrap of the prelaunch hero label at desktop width.
critical_code_review_comments: StreakDialog: caching the selection in a ref is correct. The ref stays set while the dialog is closed, but that is harmless because Radix unmounts the content and the next open overwrites the ref.
The reduced-motion selector list now covers every streak surface. dialog.jsx forwards overlayClassName without breaking other dialogs.
SeriesStreak.js is still dense single-line JSX (maintainability only).
